name: Commercial Dry Vacuum
definition: A mains-powered commercial vacuum cleaner intended to collect ordinary dry debris through a floor tool or nozzle, hose, bag or container, filtration system and vacuum motor.
includedScope: Corded commercial dry-only tub and canister vacuum cleaners
Ordinary facility dust and debris within the exact machine and filter instructions
excludedScope: Hazardous or combustible dust without exact certification
Domestic stick, upright and central extraction systems
headline: Commercial dry vacuum types, airflow boundaries, filtration and buyer verification
description: This technical profile explains commercial dry-vacuum architecture, representative tub and canister models, filtration boundaries, comparable specification limits and procurement checks.
metaDescription: Commercial dry vacuum guide covering types, airflow, filtration, components, representative models and procurement verification.
disclaimer: This is an independent category reference, not model-specific purchasing, exposure-control, electrical-safety or repair advice. Confirm the exact product number, filter and bag configuration, approved dust, regional compliance and service terms.

keyFacts.label: System boundary
keyFacts.value: Tool, hose, bag or container, filters, motor and exhaust path
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturer documentation identifies these linked systems on reviewed commercial machines.
keyFacts.scope: Functional synthesis; layouts and service parts differ.

keyFacts.label: Performance boundary
keyFacts.value: Watts, airflow, vacuum and sound are not interchangeable measures
keyFacts.evidence: Official specifications publish different metrics and reporting points by model.
keyFacts.scope: Manufacturer-stated values; no cross-model laboratory comparison.

keyFacts.label: Commercial test framework
keyFacts.value: IEC 62885-8 addresses mains-operated commercial dry-vacuum performance measurements
keyFacts.evidence: IEC states the commercial dry-vacuum scope and connection to IEC 60335-2-69.
keyFacts.scope: Test method, not a product certification or ranking.

keyFacts.label: Dust boundary
keyFacts.value: Commercial dry-vacuum naming does not prove hazardous-dust approval
keyFacts.evidence: The reviewed safety standard and product sources require exact machine and configuration checks.
keyFacts.scope: Dust identity, atmosphere and jurisdiction remain site-specific.

systemFlow.name: Surface pickup
systemFlow.role: Interfaces with the surface and admits debris and air.
systemFlow.evidence: Official product sources list model-specific tools.

systemFlow.name: Air and debris transport
systemFlow.evidence: Reviewed machines use defined hose and tube systems.
systemFlow.scope: Diameter, length and seals are model-specific.

systemFlow.name: Primary collection
systemFlow.role: Retains most collected debris for disposal.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources publish bag or container capacities and systems.
systemFlow.scope: Nominal capacity is not achieved route capacity.

systemFlow.name: Filtration
systemFlow.componentFamily: Pre-filter, main filter and exhaust filter
systemFlow.role: Protects the motor and limits dust leaving the machine according to configuration.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturers identify filter options and stages on named products.
systemFlow.scope: No universal filter grade is implied.

systemFlow.name: Airflow generation
systemFlow.evidence: Official specifications publish motor, airflow or vacuum data.

variants.name: Compact tub vacuum
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator pulls a compact canister by hose or handle
variants.spaceConstraints: Small storage footprint; cable and hose remain in the route
variants.limitations: Small size does not establish low noise, filtration or pickup performance.
variants.evidence: TASKI go and Numatic PPR170 are documented compact commercial formats.

variants.name: Quiet commercial canister
variants.operatorRelationship: Portable canister with floor-tool work ahead of the machine
variants.spaceConstraints: Sound and cable controls matter in occupied space
variants.limitations: Published sound values require matched methods and operating state.
variants.evidence: Kärcher, Nilfisk and TASKI publish sound-related data or quiet-use positioning.

variants.name: Enhanced-filter configuration
variants.taskScale: Routes with a stated indoor-air or dust-control requirement
variants.operatorRelationship: Requires controlled bag and filter handling
variants.spaceConstraints: Replacement stock and disposal workflow become part of the system
variants.limitations: A HEPA option or family label does not prove the delivered configuration or exposure-control result.
variants.evidence: Manufacturers distinguish optional and model-specific filtration arrangements.
variants.scope: Exact product number, filter, seals and bag.

performanceMetrics.name: Airflow
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Indicates air volume at the stated measurement point
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: May be turbine, machine or another source-defined point
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Compare only matched methods and configurations.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official data publishes airflow for selected models.

performanceMetrics.name: Vacuum or water lift
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: It does not equal pickup at the floor tool under loading.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official data publishes vacuum or water-lift values.

performanceMetrics.name: Collection capacity
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Bag, container and usable capacities may differ
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not compare unlike capacity definitions.

performanceMetrics.name: Input power
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Rated, nominal and maximum terms may differ
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Watts alone do not establish pickup efficiency.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Reviewed sources publish motor or input power.

performanceMetrics.name: Sound, mass and reach
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Supports occupied-route, handling and outlet planning
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Sound method, accessory mass and cable definitions must match
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Catalogue values do not replace a site trial.

applicationFit.evidence: Manufacturers position reviewed dry vacuums for commercial facility routes.
applicationFit.scope: Ordinary dry debris on approved surfaces.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Route productivity depends on tool result, outlet spacing, cable handling and bag changes.
applicationFit.basis: Reviewed architecture and official commercial positioning.
applicationFit.limitations: No independent productivity comparison was reviewed.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Trial a representative route and record cleaning result, stops, cable moves and consumables.

applicationFit.evidence: Official sources identify commercial indoor-use contexts and quiet operation for selected models.
applicationFit.scope: Named models and approved regional configurations.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Sound, exhaust quality, cable visibility and storage matter as much as nominal power.
applicationFit.basis: Published data and occupied-space use cases.
applicationFit.limitations: Site acoustics and operating practices vary.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Conduct an occupied-area trial and approve sound, cable and storage controls.

applicationFit.evidence: Reviewed products include multi-surface floor tools or commercial floor-cleaning kits.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Floor-tool geometry and achieved pickup should be tested on the actual surface mix.
applicationFit.basis: Tool architecture and IEC performance-method boundary.
applicationFit.limitations: Airflow and vacuum values alone do not predict surface result.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Test every representative carpet and hard-floor surface with the delivered tool.

applicationFit.evidence: IEC and manufacturer information distinguish commercial vacuum safety and configuration boundaries.
applicationFit.scope: This page does not classify dust or certify a machine.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Ordinary dry-vacuum naming is insufficient for exposure or ignition-risk control.
applicationFit.limitations: No hazardous-dust approval is established here.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Classify the dust and atmosphere, then obtain written approval and certification for the exact machine.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Achieved result, sound, reach and handling
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Ranking by watts or catalogue sound alone
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official data shows different power, sound and reach boundaries.
procurementDecisions.assessment: A route trial should determine outlet moves, cable controls, tool result and operator acceptance.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Catalogue metrics do not predict total route time.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Run a timed route trial with the delivered tool and consumables.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm circuit, cable, hose, seals, bag and filter part numbers.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Dust classification and complete filtration configuration
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Treating an optional HEPA label as delivered-system proof
procurementDecisions.evidence: Sources distinguish exact filters, options and safety scope.
procurementDecisions.scope: Exact dust, machine, filter, bag and jurisdiction.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Selection requires written configuration and exposure-control evidence.
procurementDecisions.limitations: This profile establishes no exposure-control result.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Obtain exact certification, filtration details and change procedure before purchase.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Verify filter grade, seals, bag closure, exhaust path and service method.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Tool compatibility and pickup on every representative surface
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Assuming one combination tool is optimal everywhere
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources list distinct tools and commercial kits.
procurementDecisions.assessment: The floor-tool package should be specified with the machine.
procurementDecisions.basis: Pickup occurs at the complete tool-airflow interface.
procurementDecisions.limitations: No universal tool result was reviewed.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Approve tools through hard-floor, carpet, edge and detail trials.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Match tool width, coupling, tube, airflow path and replacement codes.

engineeringChecks.reason: Voltage, plug, cord length and strain relief vary by market.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Confirm exact product number and site circuit before deployment.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official sources publish regional electrical data.

engineeringChecks.reason: Filter and bag choice changes dust handling and ongoing cost.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: List every consumable part number, price, stock and change method.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manufacturer sources identify model-specific filter and bag systems.

engineeringChecks.reason: Leaks, blockages and unmatched tools change achieved pickup.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Inspect hose, cuffs, seals, filters and tool interfaces during acceptance.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Reviewed systems depend on linked airflow components.

engineeringChecks.reason: Ordinary commercial dry vacuums may be inappropriate for hazardous or combustible dust.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Obtain a competent site assessment and exact machine approval.
engineeringChecks.evidence: IEC safety scope and product configuration boundaries require task-specific confirmation.

standards.name: IEC 60335-2-69:2021
standards.applicability: Particular safety requirements for wet and dry vacuum cleaners, including power-brush equipment, for commercial use.
standards.evidence: IEC publishes the commercial vacuum safety scope.
standards.scope: Confirm regional adoption and exact product conformity.

standards.name: IEC 62885-8:2019
standards.applicability: Methods for measuring performance of mains-operated commercial dry vacuum cleaners, including water-filter types.
standards.evidence: IEC states the scope and relationship to IEC 60335-2-69.
standards.scope: Measurement framework; not a product ranking or cordless-vacuum method.

developments.title: Commercial vacuum safety edition published
developments.summary: IEC published edition 6.0 of IEC 60335-2-69 for commercial wet and dry vacuum safety.
developments.evidence: The IEC catalogue records the publication and scope.
developments.scope: International base standard; local adoption differs.

developments.title: Commercial dry-vacuum performance method published
developments.summary: IEC published IEC 62885-8 for mains-operated commercial dry-vacuum performance measurements.
developments.evidence: The IEC catalogue records the publication scope.
developments.scope: Test method, not a minimum-performance requirement.
